interest: SCAP allowed industrial explosives for mining while barring export production; a citizen asks about shipping a shotgun.
overview: This file (decimal 894.113) documents United States and Allied occupation policies governing explosives, firearms, and munitions in Japan between November 1946 and January 1948. The primary focus of the records is the regulation and authorization of industrial explosives production—such as dynamite, black powder, and blasting caps—necessary for Japan's domestic economic rehabilitation while strictly enforcing demilitarization policies under JCS 1380/15 and Far Eastern Commission guidelines to prevent regional strategic dependency. The file contains policy memoranda between the State Department and the War Department regarding SCAP's inquiries about exporting surplus explosives to neighboring Asian countries, formal GHQ SCAP directives (SCAPIN 1836) establishing strict 1948 industrial production quotas, routine public correspondence concerning private sporting arms export regulations, and internal departmental records management charge-out sheets.

subfiles.about: Evaluates SCAP's inquiry regarding the export of surplus Japanese industrial explosives to neighboring Pacific and Asian countries in light of FEC disarmament policies.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman (Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Roswell H. Whitman concludes SCAP may export only normal surplus of industrial explosives, not production planned for export.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Whitman on Export of Explosives from Japan

subfiles.about: Recommends approval of a draft cable to SCAP regarding policy on exporting industrial explosives.
subfiles.summary: Philander P. Claxton Jr. sends Hilldring a draft cable limiting Japanese explosives exports to normal surplus, with War Department concurrence.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Claxton to Hilldring on Export of Explosives from Japan

subfiles.about: Reports Japanese industrial explosive capacities and requirements while requesting policy clarification on exporting small surpluses to neighboring countries.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: SCAP reports neighbors' requests for Japanese industrial explosives and asks whether surpluses may be exported or production expanded under JCS 1380/15.
subfiles.title: Telegram C 67250 from SCAP Tokyo on Industrial Explosives Exports

subfiles.about: Inquires about shipping expenses and regulations for sending a shotgun to Japan.
subfiles.summary: A private citizen writes to the Secretary of State inquiring about regulations, payment, and shipment logistics for a shotgun. The handwritten letter mentions expenses incurred and requests advice from the Department before proceeding with shipment. The State Department subsequently routed the inquiry to the Munitions Division.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mrs. Murray Requesting Advice on Shipping Shotgun to Japan

subfiles.about: Advises that no license or State Department permit is required to export a shotgun from the United States to Japan.
subfiles.summary: E. T. Cummins of the Munitions Division tells Mrs. Carl M. Murray no export license is needed to send a shotgun to Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Munitions Division to Mrs. Murray Regarding Shotgun Export

subfiles.about: Records the temporary withdrawal of a 1945 file document from the State Department archives.
subfiles.summary: Charge-out sheet for document 894.113/5-2845, charged to Miss Davis in New York on May 11, 1954.
subfiles.title: Document Charge-Out Sheet for File 894.113

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of SCAPIN 1836 authorizing the manufacture of industrial explosives and accessories in Japan during 1948.
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Acting Political Adviser in Tokyo transmits SCAPIN 1836 authorizing 1948 production of industrial explosives.
subfiles.title: Despatch from US Political Adviser Tokyo Transmitting SCAP Directive on Explosives

subfiles.about: Authorizes specific types and quantities of industrial explosives and accessories to be manufactured in Japan during 1948.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1836 authorizes Japan to make 18,900 metric tons of industrial explosives and accessories in 1948, under Eighth Army factory permits.
subfiles.title: SCAP Memorandum SCAPIN 1836 on Manufacture of Industrial Explosives and Accessories
